cmd.root.long:
roji - Reverse proxy for local development

Automatically discovers Docker Compose services and makes them accessible via *.localhost with HTTPS.
cmd.root.flag.network: Docker network name(s) to watch (comma-separated for multiple)

cmd.health.long: Performs a health check against the local roji instance. Exits with 0 if healthy, 1 otherwise.
cmd.routes.long: Display all currently registered routes from the running roji server.
cmd.doctor.short: Check system environment for common issues
cmd.doctor.long:
Check your system environment for common issues that may prevent roji from working correctly.

The doctor command runs a series of diagnostic checks:
  - Docker daemon status
  - Docker socket accessibility
  - Docker network existence
  - Port availability (80, 443)
  - CA certificate status
  - Server certificate validity
  - DNS resolution for *.localhost

Use --fix to automatically fix issues where possible.
cmd.doctor.title: roji doctor
cmd.doctor.hint.fix: Run 'roji doctor --fix' to auto-fix where possible.
cmd.ca.long:
Manage the roji Certificate Authority (CA) certificate.

The CA certificate is used to sign server certificates for HTTPS.
Installing it into your system's trust store allows browsers to
trust roji-generated certificates without warnings.

Commands:
  status    - Check CA certificate installation status
  install   - Install CA certificate to system trust store
  uninstall - Remove CA certificate from system trust store
  export    - Export CA certificate to a file
cmd.ca.install.short: Install CA certificate to system trust store
cmd.ca.install.long:
Install the roji CA certificate to the system trust store.

This allows browsers and other applications to trust HTTPS certificates
generated by roji without showing security warnings.

On macOS:
  - Installs to System Keychain (requires sudo)
  - Use --user to install to login keychain (no sudo)

On Linux:
  - Installs to system CA store (requires sudo)
  - Use --firefox to also install to Firefox's NSS store

On Linux (WSL):
  - Use --windows to install to Windows certificate store
  - Use --windows --user to install to Windows user store (no admin)

On Windows:
  - Installs to Machine certificate store (requires admin)
  - Use --user to install to User certificate store (no admin)
cmd.ca.install.flag.user: Install to user store instead of system store (macOS/Windows only)
cmd.ca.install.flag.firefox: Also install to Firefox's certificate store (Linux only, requires nss-tools)
cmd.ca.install.flag.windows: Install to Windows certificate store (WSL only)
cmd.ca.install.flag.force: Force install even if a certificate with the same name exists
cmd.ca.install.wsl_only: --windows flag is only available on WSL
cmd.ca.install.restart_hint: You may need to restart your browser for changes to take effect.
cmd.ca.uninstall.short: Remove CA certificate from system trust store
cmd.ca.uninstall.long:
Remove the roji CA certificate from the system trust store.

This revokes the trust for roji-generated HTTPS certificates.
cmd.ca.uninstall.flag.user: Remove from user store instead of system store (macOS/Windows only)
cmd.ca.uninstall.flag.firefox: Also remove from Firefox's certificate store (Linux only)
cmd.ca.uninstall.flag.windows: Remove from Windows certificate store (WSL only)
cmd.ca.uninstall.no_file: Cannot uninstall without the original certificate file.
cmd.ca.uninstall.wsl_only: --windows flag is only available on WSL
cmd.ca.uninstall.not_installed: CA certificate is not installed in system trust store
cmd.ca.uninstall.restart_hint: You may need to restart your browser for changes to take effect.
cmd.ca.export.short: Export CA certificate to a file
cmd.ca.export.long:
Export the roji CA certificate to a file.

Supported formats (determined by file extension):
  .pem  - PEM format (default, used by most Unix systems)
  .crt  - DER format (used by Windows)
  .cer  - DER format (alternative extension)

If no path is specified, exports to the current directory as roji-ca.pem.

Examples:
  roji ca export                    # Export as ./roji-ca.pem
  roji ca export ~/roji-ca.pem     # Export to home directory
  roji ca export ca.crt            # Export in DER format for Windows
cmd.ca.export.der_hint:
This is a DER-encoded certificate (binary format).
On Windows, double-click to install, or use:
  certutil -addstore ROOT %s
cmd.ca.export.pem_hint:
This is a PEM-encoded certificate (text format).
Import this file into your browser or OS trust store.

cmd.service.short: Manage roji as a system service
cmd.service.long:
Manage roji as a system service.

Supported platforms:
  - Linux: systemd (/etc/systemd/system/roji.service)
  - macOS: launchd (~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.roji.agent.plist)
  - Windows: NSSM (requires NSSM from https://nssm.cc/)

Linux requires root privileges (use sudo).
macOS runs as a user-level service (no sudo required).
Windows requires Administrator privileges.
cmd.service.install.short: Install roji as a system service
cmd.service.install.long:
Install roji as a system service.

On Linux, this creates a systemd service unit and enables it to start on boot.
Requires root privileges (use sudo).
cmd.service.install.flag.user: User to run the service as (default: current user)
cmd.service.uninstall.long:
Uninstall roji system service.

This stops the service (if running), disables auto-start, and removes the service configuration.
Requires root privileges (use sudo).
cmd.service.status.title: roji service status
cmd.service.status.install_hint: Run 'sudo roji service install' to install the service.
cmd.log.long:
View roji server logs from the log file.

By default, follows the log file in real-time (like tail -f).
Use --no-follow to print current logs and exit.
